assessment.summary: BRAF (P15056) is one of the most extensively characterised and validated oncology drug targets in human biology, with 5 approved small-molecule inhibitors, over 11,000 IC50 measurements in ChEMBL, and 138 PDB structures including many at high resolution with ligands bound. The evidence overwhelmingly supports high druggability across structural, chemical, and literature dimensions, with well-established disease relevance particularly in melanoma, colorectal cancer, and thyroid cancer driven by the V600E mutation.
evidence_gaps: AlphaFold mean pLDDT of 66.4 is relatively low (though this is superseded by abundant experimental PDB data, so it is not a practical concern)

Resistance mechanisms to current BRAF inhibitors (e.g., paradoxical MAPK activation, splice variants, RAS mutations) remain an active clinical challenge, limiting utility of current drugs in certain contexts
Structural coverage of clinically relevant resistance mutants and non-V600 BRAF mutants may be incomplete
Pan-RAF and BRAF dimer inhibition (next-generation approaches) may require further structural and chemical optimisation
Efficacy data in RAS wild-type contexts (where paradoxical activation occurs) is limited and context-dependent
